title: 1946 London County Council election
summary: The first London County Council election after the Second World War produced a Labour landslide, mirroring the party's 1945 general election triumph. Labour won 90 of the 124 elected seats on 55.0% of the vote, with the anti-socialist Municipal Reform bloc reduced to 30. The Liberals returned to the council in Bethnal Green and the Communists won their only ever LCC seats in Mile End. Turnout was very low at 26.4% so soon after the war.
highlights: The Municipal Reform (Conservative) bloc falls to 30 seats
Percy Harris and Edward Martell win Bethnal Green for the Liberals; the Communists take both Mile End seats — the CPGB's only LCC seats

council.note: 124 directly elected councillors, plus aldermen chosen by the council. The main anti-Labour party at this election was the Municipal Reform Party; the Conservatives stood under their own name from 1949. The Elections Centre compendium credits all 94 non-Conservative seats to Labour, but contemporary reports (The Times, 9 March 1946) record 90 Labour, 2 Liberal (Bethnal Green) and 2 Communist (Mile End) — the attribution used here. Liberal and Communist vote totals are the sums of all their candidates' bloc votes as reported by The Times; their vote shares are omitted because the main-party percentages use the Elections Centre's best-placed-candidate basis.
council.otherVotesNote: Under the multi-member bloc vote each elector had as many votes as seats to fill; minor-party totals and shares are as recorded in the Elections Centre compendium and contemporary press reports, whose percentage bases differ slightly.

sources.label: Rallings & Thrasher, London County Council Elections 1889–1961 (Elections Centre)
